newsitem.title: UK: UK financial services unruffled by EMU doubts.
newsitem.headline: UK financial services unruffled by EMU doubts.

text.p: Britain's financial services industry believes it can compete successfully whether Britain joins a single European currency or not, said Pat Newberry, senior member of Coopers & Lybrand's consulting practice.

"The doubts and rows about EMU are not shaking confidence," he told a press conference. "Financial services firms believe they can compete effectively when EMU comes in," he said, at the launch of a quarterly survey of UK financial services, conducted by Coopers & Lybrand and the Confederation of British Industry.

Both the Conservative government and the opposition Labour Party have said they will keep their options open on signing up for European Economic and Monetary Union in the first round, due to start on January 1, 1999.
Newberry said EMU was "on companies' radar screens" but had yet to show up in investment plans.
Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis, said keeping Britain's EMU option open was the right course of action.
